title: Completeness of ambient internal Hom in the fixed integral presentation
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite field extension, and $X$ a scheme. Put $B_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and use the ordinary unbounded derived categories and ambient relative derived internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $F_X$ be the fixed composite of the section-action derived equivalence [def-sfb-integral-section-action-transport], the quotient-normalized detailed coefficient transport and restriction along the completed coefficient isomorphism [def-sfb-integral-completed-coefficient-transport]. This reads the same object over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$, without applying completion. Let $I$ be the ideal generated by the chosen uniformizer, and use the local-completeness and fixed-scalar residue predicates [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. For any $K,L\in D(B_X)$, if $F_X(L)$ is locally derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete], then so is $F_X(R\mathcal Hom_{B_X}(K,L))$. No constructibility, boundedness, field-of-definition, or perfectness assumption is imposed on either input beyond completeness of the second.

proof.text: Apply the module-object/ringed-site comparison to the spectral integral coefficient ring. It identifies the ambient module-object internal Hom with the K-injective ringed-site internal Hom, naturally in both inputs, and compatibly with restriction to every slice and evaluation.

The coefficient maps in F_X are ring isomorphisms. Exact scalar restriction along each is an equivalence, so the tensor-Hom adjunction identifies transport of Hom with Hom of the transported inputs. These ring maps preserve all positive quotient projections; consequently they preserve the kernel ideal of the first projection. Pass to the equivalent small site in the definition of IsSfbAdicComplete. Termwise exact equivalences and the universal property of localization compare the recorded derived universes as well.

Apply the ringed-site derived Hom completeness theorem to the kernel ideal and the transported second argument. For every slice and ideal section f, currying and symmetry identify Hom(O[1/f],Hom(K,L)) with Hom(K,Hom(O[1/f],L)). Its inner Hom is zero by completeness. Exact equivalences preserve zero and the slice comparisons transport all these local tests back, giving exactly the conclusion.

theorem integralAdicHom_complete
    (K L : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X))
    (hL : Scheme.IsSfbAdicComplete X (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E).ideal
      (((integralSectionDerivedEquivalence l E X).functor ⋙
        Scheme.integralDetailedTransport X l E ⋙
        Scheme.pbcDerivedRestrict (Scheme.pbcCompletedComparison X
          (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E)).hom).obj L)) :
    Scheme.IsSfbAdicComplete X (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E).ideal
      (((integralSectionDerivedEquivalence l E X).functor ⋙
        Scheme.integralDetailedTransport X l E ⋙
        Scheme.pbcDerivedRestrict (Scheme.pbcCompletedComparison X
          (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E)).hom).obj
        (((CondensedRing.derivedHom (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X).obj
        (op K)).obj L))
